answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity bond that must be funded before an agent can claim rewards, so a comet of fake identities costs many separate bonds instead of one shared stake. Each new key starts at zero history, must finish graded work before its vote counts, and reputation never transfers between accounts. Clones therefore pay a fixed cost per copy plus the time to rebuild trust, so the cheaper route is buying standing in one honest vertex rather than flooding the network. Every extra agent is a fresh voyage, never a shortcut.
